To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the frequency dependence of the loss is reduced by applying a sinusoidal or a triangular B(t), and that the total loss of HPT deformed amorphous Fe75Al25 is independent of the frequency when a triangular induction B is applied.
the frequency dependence of the loss of soft magnetic materials depends on the H(t) shape.
the shape of the applied H(t) or B(t) has a strong influence on the total core loss, and the frequency dependence of the loss becomes smaller for triangular B(t).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the H(t) and the B(t) shape on the hysteres is loop and loss measurements of soft magnetic materials.
the frequency dependence of core losses and hysteresis loops of soft magnetic materials.
the influence of the shape of H(t) and/or B(t) on hysteresis and loss measurements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the shape of the induction B(t) is more important for the loss measurements of soft magnetic materials than the shape of the magnetic field H(t).
the frequency dependence of the total loss of the materials investigated is strongly dependent on the H(t) shape, but the B(t) shape has only a minor influence.
the hystereses and the loss measurements of soft magnetic materials should be carried out with a triangular B(t) to minimize the frequency dependence and to obtain a reliable loss value.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the total loss W is independent of H(t) and frequency when a triangular induction B (t) is applied.
the frequency dependence of the core loss is determined by the frequency dependence of B(t) and H(t).
the total loss W and the loss separation model are strongly dependent on the shape of the applied field H(t) and induction B(t) in soft magnetic materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the frequency dependence of the loss in soft magnetic materials is strongly dependent on the H(t) and, especially, the B(t) shape, and the microstructure of the material.
for a given material, a triangular B(t) is more appropriate to measure the core loss than the sinusoidal B(t).
for a given material the frequency dependence of the loss can be changed by changing either the shape of H(t) or that of B(t).
